summary: Defines an ENUM NAPTR record type for Internet fax (IFax) service. DNS returns the email address of the target IFax system, so a sender can use a telephone number to reach it instead of needing to know the address in advance. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC registers a way to find an Internet fax email address from a telephone number. It also says that a person must give informed consent before their information is published in ENUM.

questions: send fax using phone number via dns
what is the e2u+ifax enum service
subtitle: The E2U+ifax ENUM service lets a telephone number resolve to an email address for Internet fax.

tldr.problem: A sender using Internet mail for fax may know the recipient's telephone number but not the recipient system's email address.
tldr.mechanism: An IFax client queries DNS through ENUM with the telephone number and uses the email address returned in a NAPTR record.
tldr.outcome: The RFC registers the E2U+ifax service and requires explicit informed consent before data is published in ENUM. The unit metadata says RFC 6118 updates it.

today: The unit metadata says RFC 4143 is updated by RFC 6118. RFC 4143 is a Standards Track document that registers an ENUM service for Internet fax.

sections.title: Finding an Internet Fax Address
sections.content:
IFax means facsimile using Internet mail. An IFax client makes an ENUM DNS query using the target system's telephone number. The returned Naming Authority Pointer (NAPTR) record gives an email address for reaching that system.

The address is then used with Simple Mode, Extended Facsimile using Internet Mail, or the Full Mode Fax Profile for Internet Mail, as named in RFC 3965, RFC 2532 and RFC 4142.
sections.plainLanguage: The client looks up a telephone number in ENUM and gets an email address for Internet fax. The sender can then use that address with an Internet mail fax method.

sections.title: The E2U+ifax Registration
sections.content:
The registered service name is E2U+ifax. Its type is ifax, its subtype is mailto, and its URI scheme is mailto. The RFC explains that Internet fax is a profile of standard Internet mail and uses standard mail addressing.

The intended usage is COMMON. The registration is made under the terms of RFC 3761.
sections.plainLanguage: The registration tells ENUM that the service is Internet fax and that the lookup result is a mailto address. That address is used with standard Internet mail.

sections.title: Example NAPTR Record
sections.content: The RFC shows an example NAPTR record under a reversed telephone-number domain in e164.arpa. Its service field is E2U+ifax:mailto, and its rewrite rule produces mailto:toyo@example.com.
sections.plainLanguage: The example shows a directory record returning an email address that begins with mailto:.

sections.title: Privacy and Consent
sections.content:
ENUM uses DNS, a globally distributed database whose stored information is visible anonymously. The RFC warns that published telephone numbers and IFax information could be collected automatically and used to send junk faxes.

Because a published telephone number cannot easily be replaced with a separate disposable number, the RFC states that the data subject MUST give explicit informed consent before data is published in ENUM. The security considerations in the referenced fax and ENUM specifications also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Anyone can read information published in DNS, so a listed fax number could attract junk faxes. The person whose data is listed must give informed consent first.
